_comment: Shot manifest for the Fundamentals series. Each entry generates a placeholder PNG into <lab>/images/<file>. Backfill by overwriting the PNG — no markdown changes needed. Run: python make-placeholders.py

lab-00-concepts.title: The editor, annotated
lab-00-concepts.spec: Full editor window, a medium-sized flow open (motor-interlock is a good choice). Four numbered callouts: 1 node palette, 2 canvas, 3 inspector, 4 simulator panel (docked, collapsed is fine).
lab-00-concepts.alt: The SMFlow editor with the node palette, canvas, inspector, and simulator panel labelled

lab-00-concepts.title: The scan cycle
lab-00-concepts.spec: DIAGRAM, not a screenshot. Snapshot inputs -> run due tasks -> commit outputs -> diagnostics -> wait. Vertical flow, arrow looping back to the top. Match the ASCII version in the lab text.
lab-00-concepts.alt: The scan cycle: snapshot inputs, run due tasks, commit outputs, diagnostics, wait for next tick

lab-00-concepts.title: Why a mid-scan change isn't seen
lab-00-concepts.spec: DIAGRAM. Timeline with scan boundaries. An input pin transitions 2 ms into a scan; mark clearly that the logic reads the snapshot taken at the boundary, and the change is only picked up at the NEXT boundary. This is the most important picture in Lab 0 — give it room.
lab-00-concepts.alt: Timeline showing an input changing mid-scan and not being seen until the next scan boundary

lab-00-concepts.title: Task configuration
lab-00-concepts.spec: The task configuration dialog or inspector pane, showing Name, Kind, Period, Priority, Budget. Kind picker open if possible, so Normal / Init / Interrupt are all visible.
lab-00-concepts.frame: Dialog, cropped tight with a little surrounding canvas for context
lab-00-concepts.alt: The task configuration dialog showing name, kind, period, priority, and budget

lab-00-concepts.title: Two tasks, one tick
lab-00-concepts.spec: DIAGRAM. A 10 ms task and a 25 ms task on a shared 5 ms tick line. Mark every tick; mark which ticks each task fires on (10/20/30... and 25/50/75...). Caption the tick as GCD(10,25) = 5.
lab-00-concepts.alt: A 10 ms and a 25 ms task scheduled on a shared 5 ms tick

lab-00-concepts.title: Anatomy of a node
lab-00-concepts.spec: One node on the canvas, zoomed, with the inspector beside it. Callouts: input ports, output ports, and properties (in the inspector). A compare or ton node works well since it has both.
lab-00-concepts.alt: A node with its input ports, output ports, and inspector properties labelled

lab-00-concepts.title: A refused connection
lab-00-concepts.spec: Mid-drag: a float32 output being dragged toward an int32 input, with the editor's refusal affordance visible (cursor state / port styling / tooltip). Capture the moment the editor says no, not the aftermath.
lab-00-concepts.frame: Two nodes and the wire being dragged between them
lab-00-concepts.alt: The editor refusing a connection between a float32 output and an int32 input

lab-00-concepts.title: Declaring a shared variable
lab-00-concepts.spec: The variable configuration dialog: Name, Type, Initial value, Persistence. Set persistence to Retained so the retention option is visible.
lab-00-concepts.alt: The variable configuration dialog with name, type, initial value, and persistence

lab-00-concepts.title: Logical names, per-target bindings
lab-00-concepts.spec: DIAGRAM. One logical name (StopButton) on the left, fanning out to three target bindings: opta -> I2, rp2040-pico -> gpio17, simulator -> virtual point. Make the point that the graph side never changes.
lab-00-concepts.alt: One logical I/O name binding to different physical pins on three different targets

lab-00-concepts.title: smflow targets
lab-00-concepts.spec: Terminal, 18pt, running `smflow targets` with the full list visible. Light terminal theme.
lab-00-concepts.frame: Terminal only, cropped to the command and its output
lab-00-concepts.alt: Terminal output of the smflow targets command listing supported boards

lab-00-concepts.title: Declaring a peripheral
lab-00-concepts.spec: The peripheral configuration UI with an SSD1306 declared: instance name and part type. If a bus/address field is shown, include it.
lab-00-concepts.frame: Dialog or inspector pane, tight crop
lab-00-concepts.alt: Declaring an SSD1306 display as a named peripheral

lab-00-concepts.title: The build report
lab-00-concepts.spec: The generated build-report.txt open in an editor or printed to terminal. Must show the Tasks table, the RAM (Application State) line, and the Stack Frame Depth 'bounded (flat scan loop)' line.
lab-00-concepts.frame: Full report, readable at 720p; crop the file-sizes section if needed for legibility
lab-00-concepts.alt: A SMFlow build report showing task periods, memory use, and bounded stack depth

lab-00-concepts.title: A diagnostic, highlighted on the canvas
lab-00-concepts.spec: The editor showing a validation error in the diagnostics list AND the offending node highlighted on the canvas. The link between the two is the point of the shot.
lab-00-concepts.alt: A validation error in the diagnostics panel with the offending node highlighted on the canvas

lab-00-concepts.title: The whole pipeline
lab-00-concepts.spec: DIAGRAM. .smflow -> validation -> typed IR -> lowering -> C++ -> native binary, vertical, with the failure branch off validation. Match the ASCII version in the lab text.
lab-00-concepts.alt: The SMFlow compilation pipeline from project file to native binary

lab-01-first-flow.title: The payoff, up front
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Full-frame generated application.cpp for the NOT gate, syntax highlit, nothing else in shot. This is the same image the video cold-opens on. Must be legible on a phone.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The generated application.cpp containing two lines: a bool local and io.Motor = !startButton

lab-01-first-flow.title: A new, empty project
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Editor just after File > New Project. Empty canvas, palette on the left, and the default Main task visible in the task list or inspector with its 10 ms period.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: A newly created empty SMFlow project with a default Main task

lab-01-first-flow.title: Finding the node
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Node palette with the I/O category expanded and Digital Input hovered or selected. Include enough canvas to show where it is about to be dropped.
lab-01-first-flow.frame: Palette plus left third of canvas
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The node palette with the I/O category expanded and Digital Input selected

lab-01-first-flow.title: Naming matters
lab-01-first-flow.spec: The Digital Input node selected, inspector open, Name field being set to StartButton. The name should be visible on the node on the canvas too.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: Renaming a Digital Input node to StartButton in the inspector

lab-01-first-flow.title: Three nodes, not yet wired
lab-01-first-flow.spec: StartButton, NOT, and Motor placed left to right, no wires yet. Clean spacing. This is the 'before' half of a before/after pair with 1.06.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: Three unconnected nodes: StartButton, NOT, and Motor

lab-01-first-flow.title: Drawing a wire
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Mid-drag from StartButton.value toward NOT.in, with whatever the editor shows for a valid target port (highlight / snap). Catch it in motion.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: Dragging a connection from the StartButton value port to the NOT input port

lab-01-first-flow.title: The finished flow
lab-01-first-flow.spec: All three nodes wired. This image gets reused in the series index and the video thumbnail, so compose it properly: centered, generous margins, nothing selected.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The completed flow: StartButton wired through a NOT node to Motor

lab-01-first-flow.title: Valid
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Terminal running `smflow validate lab-01.smflow` and printing `Lab 01 - First Flow: valid.`
lab-01-first-flow.frame: Terminal, cropped to command and output
lab-01-first-flow.alt: Terminal showing smflow validate reporting the project is valid

lab-01-first-flow.title: It works
lab-01-first-flow.spec: The simulator panel with StartButton toggled ON and Motor showing OFF. If the panel shows a scan counter, let it be a non-round number so it reads as genuinely running.
lab-01-first-flow.frame: Simulator panel plus enough canvas for context
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The simulator panel showing StartButton on and Motor off

lab-01-first-flow.title: Five files
lab-01-first-flow.spec: File explorer or `ls` of the generated/ directory showing application.cpp, application.h, hardware.cpp, hardware.h, main.cpp.
lab-01-first-flow.frame: Terminal or file tree, tight crop
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The generated directory containing five C++ source files

lab-01-first-flow.title: Your logic
lab-01-first-flow.spec: application.cpp full frame with MainTask visible in full. Optionally annotate: an arrow from the graph's node names to the identifiers in the code. Large type.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The generated MainTask function assigning io.Motor from the negated startButton

lab-01-first-flow.title: Nothing there
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Terminal, the grep for Node|Graph|ExecuteNode|Runtime|Interpreter|ScriptEngine over generated/, returning nothing. Show the command AND the empty result AND the next prompt, so it reads as a completed search rather than a hung one.
lab-01-first-flow.frame: Terminal, cropped to command and prompt
lab-01-first-flow.alt: A grep for runtime and interpreter terms across the generated sources returning no matches

lab-01-first-flow.title: The scan loop
lab-01-first-flow.spec: main.cpp scrolled to the while loop in main(). Highlight or annotate ReadInputs and WriteOutputs.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The generated scan loop calling ReadInputs, MainTask, and WriteOutputs

lab-01-first-flow.title: Byte-identical
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Terminal showing the two builds and `diff -r build-a build-b` returning nothing, followed by a clean prompt. Same 'completed, not hung' consideration as 1.12.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: A recursive diff of two separate builds showing no differences

lab-01-first-flow.title: It refuses
lab-01-first-flow.spec: Terminal with the SMF0005 error text in full. Pair with 1.16.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: Terminal showing error SMF0005, a required input is not connected

lab-01-first-flow.title: Which node
lab-01-first-flow.spec: The same error in the editor's diagnostics panel, with the Motor node highlighted on the canvas and its unconnected input port visibly flagged.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: The Motor node highlighted on the canvas with its unconnected input flagged

lab-01-first-flow.title: The exercise solution
lab-01-first-flow.spec: The four-node AND version: StartButton and GuardClosed into an AND node into Motor. Wired and valid.
lab-01-first-flow.alt: StartButton and GuardClosed wired into an AND node driving Motor

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: The finished Lab 2 flow
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: All ten nodes wired: three inputs on the left, the motor chain and the alarm chain running right. Lay it out so the two chains are visually distinct and the GuardClosed fan-out is obvious. Reused in the thumbnail.
lab-02-scan-cycle.frame: Canvas only, hero composition, nothing selected
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: The completed Lab 2 graph with ten nodes and two output chains

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: One output, two destinations
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: Tight on the GuardClosed node with both its outgoing wires visible — one to the ready AND, one to the noguard NOT. Highlight or thicken both wires if the editor allows selection highlighting.
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: Both output chains wired, with GuardClosed fanning out to two destinations

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: One input, two effects
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: Simulator with StartButton on and GuardClosed OFF. Motor must read off and Alarm must read on, both visible in the same frame — that simultaneity is the point.
lab-02-scan-cycle.frame: Simulator panel, both outputs in frame
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: The simulator with the guard open, showing the motor stopped and the alarm active

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: Ten nodes, two expressions
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: Full-frame generated MainTask: three const bool reads and two assignments. Consider a side-by-side or inset with the ten-node graph to make the collapse land. Large type.
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: The generated MainTask with three locals and two assignments

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: Layout is not semantics
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: Split frame. Left: the canvas deliberately rearranged into a mess (outputs on the left, nodes overlapping). Right: the identical generated code, or the empty output of `diff -r before after`. The diff must show no output with a clean prompt after it.
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: A deliberately messy canvas layout beside the unchanged generated code

lab-02-scan-cycle.title: A cycle refuses to build
lab-02-scan-cycle.spec: The SMF0007 error naming notjam, run, and motor. Ideally paired with the editor showing the feedback wire that caused it. Include the full message — the 'feedback loops require a state-bearing node' sentence is the teaching part.
lab-02-scan-cycle.frame: Terminal, or terminal plus canvas inset
lab-02-scan-cycle.alt: The SMF0007 cycle error naming the three nodes in the loop

lab-03-tasks.title: Three tasks on one canvas
lab-03-tasks.spec: The nine nodes arranged so the three tasks read as three groups. If the editor tints or labels nodes by task, make sure that is visible. The absence of any wire between the Control and Report groups is the thing to see.
lab-03-tasks.alt: The Lab 3 graph with three tasks shown as separate groups on the canvas

lab-03-tasks.title: Declaring three tasks
lab-03-tasks.spec: The task panel or task list showing all three: Startup (init, no period), Control (10 ms), Report (250 ms). If the kind picker can be shown open on Startup, better.
lab-03-tasks.alt: The task configuration panel listing Startup as init, Control at 10 ms, and Report at 250 ms

lab-03-tasks.title: Two rates, visibly
lab-03-tasks.spec: Hard shot, worth the effort: the simulator at an instant where Motor has already changed and StatusLamp has not. Step the simulator rather than running it free if that makes the moment catchable. A scan counter in frame helps sell it.
lab-03-tasks.frame: Simulator panel with both outputs and, if available, the scan counter
lab-03-tasks.alt: The simulator showing Motor already on while StatusLamp has not yet updated

lab-03-tasks.title: One function per task
lab-03-tasks.spec: Generated application.cpp showing StartupTask, ControlTask, and ReportTask together. Scroll position matters — get all three function signatures in one frame even if bodies are partly cut.

lab-03-tasks.title: Atomic by construction
lab-03-tasks.spec: LoadShared_Running and StoreShared_Running with their EnterCritical/ExitCritical pairs. Highlight the critical section calls.
lab-03-tasks.alt: The generated shared-variable accessors with critical sections

lab-03-tasks.title: The whole scheduler
lab-03-tasks.spec: main.cpp: kTickMs = 10 and the while loop with both modulo-guarded task calls. Annotate the tick constant and the two moduli. If the init task call above the loop fits in frame, include it.
lab-03-tasks.alt: The generated scan loop with two modulo-guarded task calls

lab-03-tasks.title: Per-task cost
lab-03-tasks.spec: The build report Tasks table. Startup must show 'init' in the Period column where the others show times — that contrast is the point of the shot.
lab-03-tasks.alt: The build report task table showing three tasks with Startup listed as init

lab-03-tasks.title: A wire cannot cross tasks
lab-03-tasks.spec: The SMF0015 error with its full message naming both task names. Pair with the editor refusing the connection if that affordance is visible.
lab-03-tasks.frame: Terminal, or terminal plus canvas inset

lab-04-types.title: The finished Lab 4 flow
lab-04-types.spec: The full graph with TankLevel fanning out to the compare node and the to-text node. If the editor styles wires or ports by type, frame so the float32 and bool wires are distinguishable.
lab-04-types.alt: The Lab 4 graph showing the analog input feeding both a compare node and a to-text node

lab-04-types.title: An operator is a property
lab-04-types.spec: The compare node selected with its inspector showing the Operator choice list open, all six options visible. The node's a/b/out ports should also be in frame — the shot is about ports versus properties.
lab-04-types.alt: The compare node's inspector with the operator choice list open

lab-04-types.title: Ports derived from a property
lab-04-types.spec: The to-text inspector with Type float32, Decimals 1, and the format template. Frame so the node's input port is visible alongside, since the Type choice is what gave it that port type.
lab-04-types.alt: The to-text inspector showing type, decimals, and the format template

lab-04-types.title: Analog in, text out
lab-04-types.spec: Simulator with the TankLevel slider above 80, HighAlarm lit, and several formatted lines in the console pane. Let the level values be arbitrary decimals, not round numbers.
lab-04-types.frame: Simulator panel including the console output pane
lab-04-types.alt: The simulator with the analog input slider above the setpoint, the alarm lit, and formatted console output

lab-04-types.title: float stays float
lab-04-types.spec: The generated MainTask. Annotate three things: the `const float` locals, the literal `>`, and the fixed-capacity Bytes<256> buffer. May need two stacked crops to stay legible.
lab-04-types.alt: The generated MainTask showing float locals, the comparison, and the text assembly

lab-04-types.title: No implicit conversion
lab-04-types.spec: The SMF0004 error for float32 into bool. The phrase 'no implicit conversion is performed' must be legible — it is the lab's thesis in the tool's own words.
lab-04-types.alt: The SMF0004 type mismatch error for float32 into bool

lab-04-types.title: Ports are case-sensitive
lab-04-types.spec: The SMF0003 error naming the node, its type, and the port that does not exist.
lab-04-types.alt: The SMF0003 error naming the node, its type, and the missing port

lab-05-state.title: The finished Lab 5 flow
lab-05-state.spec: Nine nodes: three inputs, the set-reset latch, counter and falling-edge, three outputs. Lay out so the three state-bearing nodes (latch, counter, fe) read as the spine. If the editor marks stateful nodes distinctly, make that visible.
lab-05-state.frame: Canvas only, hero composition, nothing selected
lab-05-state.alt: The completed Lab 5 graph with a set-reset latch, counter, and falling-edge pulse

lab-05-state.title: The ladder reflex, refused
lab-05-state.spec: Split or inset: the four-node seal-in on the canvas with the feedback wire clearly looping back, and the SMF0007 error. The sentence 'Feedback loops require a state-bearing node, which does not exist yet' must be legible — the rest of the lab is its answer.
lab-05-state.frame: Canvas plus terminal or diagnostics panel
lab-05-state.alt: The seal-in attempt drawn on the canvas with the SMF0007 cycle error

lab-05-state.title: One scan wide
lab-05-state.spec: The simulator single-stepped to the exact scan where CycleEnd is true, with Motor having just gone false. A visible scan counter sells that this is one scan and not a held value. Stepping, not free-run.
lab-05-state.frame: Simulator panel, Motor and CycleEnd both in frame
lab-05-state.alt: The simulator stepped to the exact scan where CycleEnd is true

lab-05-state.title: Load, compute, store
lab-05-state.spec: Full MainTask. Annotate one state node's three lines (load state.s1_latched, compute t6, store it) to show the pattern, then let the reader see it repeat twice more. Call out `startButton || t3 && !stopButton` as the seal-in the compiler wrote.
lab-05-state.frame: Code only, 20pt+; two stacked crops if needed for legibility
lab-05-state.alt: The generated MainTask with three state loads and three state stores

lab-05-state.title: State, priced
lab-05-state.spec: Two panes if possible: the linux-x64 report Tasks table showing 7 B state, and the atmega328-uno 'RAM (Application State) 13 bytes / State: 7 B, IO: 6 B' line. The AVR one is the one that makes the number feel real.
lab-05-state.alt: The build report showing 7 bytes of application state

lab-05-state.title: State is RAM
lab-05-state.spec: Before/after pair: the simulator with the motor latched on and a count of six, then the same panel immediately after a restart showing motor off and count zero. Consider insetting the InitializeApplication function, which is the explanation.
lab-05-state.frame: Two simulator states side by side
lab-05-state.alt: Two simulator runs side by side: a count of six before restart, zero after
